name: Coinbase
summary: Candidates report a CodeSignal assessment, sometimes with aptitude and culture tests, then a recruiter call and an onsite of practical coding, system design and a hiring manager round. Recent reports also mention AI-assisted coding rounds and crypto-flavoured problems.

rounds.name: CodeSignal assessment
rounds.what: Timed online assessment; recent reports describe multi-level problems that build on each other.

rounds.name: Aptitude and culture tests
rounds.what: Some pipelines add a short cognitive aptitude test and a long personality or work-style questionnaire.

rounds.name: Recruiter call
rounds.what: Experience, interest in Coinbase and crypto, and level fit.

rounds.name: Technical coding
rounds.what: Build a small feature from input data as a pseudo project, getting as far as you can.

rounds.name: AI-assisted coding
rounds.what: Recent reports: find a bug, design a feature, review a PR and debug a production issue with AI tools allowed.

rounds.name: System design
rounds.what: Practical, product-focused service design, often microservices and their network topology.

rounds.name: Hiring manager
rounds.what: Culture and behavioural fit, including mission alignment.

tips: Practise timed, multi-level CodeSignal-style problems where each level extends the last.
Write production-quality code with clear structure and tests, not just the shortest answer.
Have a specific reason for wanting to work on crypto or financial infrastructure.
For design, expect correctness, idempotency and auditability for ledgers and orders.
If you apply to several teams, ask whether a passed CodeSignal can be reused.
